title: WITCHRIV
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Nona, a mage hiding among humans, uses magic to fix her friend's glasses and draws the attention of the Bureau of Magic Surveillance, which persecutes mages. After the Bureau kills her friend's family she is jailed with another mage, Mira-Mira, and the story turns to escape and resistance.
life_message: Refusing to submit to unjust persecution, and protecting those who share your fate, is the path to dignity.

content.note: The Bureau kills Nona's friend and family; comb magic slices people in large panels (AniTrendz; AniList Gore, MU Blood and Gore).
Persecution, imprisonment and threats; AniList Tragedy and Dystopian.
Mira-Mira has given up resisting before Nona's arrival; grief over a murdered friend (AniTrendz).
Nona threatens a guard's eye with a needle during escape.

dominant: Persecuted minority resisting a surveillance state; prejudice and class power

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Nona answers state violence with defiance and threats rather than appeals.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Story sides with escape from state surveillance and control.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to her friend and fellow mages over society at large.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Bureau hierarchy is the villain; solidarity among prisoners.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Magic is innate, neither tradition nor reason highlighted.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Fight for survival and freedom from persecution.

folkways.japan: A Shonen Jump+ dark fantasy following the Japanese web-manga witch-persecution trend; the setting is European-styled rather than Japanese.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer calls the persecution theme blunt and predictable and the Bureau one-dimensional (AniTrendz).

personified.ideology: magic is dangerous; only obedient humans deserve protection

delivery.note: The anti-prejudice message is stated plainly, and its opponents are drawn as clear villains whose case collapses (one review).

winners_losers: Persecuted mages win sympathy; the Bureau and its 'magic is dangerous' argument are shown as hypocritical.
to_verify: Strawman call rests on one review of early chapters; later arcs may add nuance.
